content.comment_body: Hello, This is my first time working with [product_name] devices, and I have some questions: 1- Can the [product_name] Communication Module (such as [product_name] CMR2040 or 2020) operate on its own, without a base module? Specifically, I need projects requiring 2 digital inputs and 2 digital outputs with SMS functionality—can the module send and receive SMS for control purposes? 2- Regarding base modules: Can any of the available 8 [product_name] modules be used as a base module? 3- Is it possible to remotely access both the base module and Communication Module using their IP address via a web browser—for example, to update some configuration?

1.) The Communication Module can operate independently. Its two digital inputs can initiate sending SMS, and its two digital outputs can be controlled via SMS. 2.) I'm not entirely clear on your question, but to clarify: the Communication Module communicates with only one [product_name] base module. If multiple base modules are present, these can be networked to exchange data, but only the one connected base module communicates with the Communication Module. 3.) Without more details on what you wish to change, I can't provide a definite answer. The Communication Module is configured using its web interface. If you're connecting to a single base module using [product_name] software, the Communication Module can route traffic. VPN access is also possible; there are relevant examples from [company_name].

Hello [user_name], Thank you. For point 2: Regarding the Communication Module working with base modules—the available [product_name] modules (with or without display), do any of these 8 modules serve as a base module? For point 3: There are two scenarios for remote management and monitoring: 3.a: When using the Communication Module alone, can we connect remotely via web browser to its IP address using a VPN? Does this mean a VPN server is built into the Communication Module? And if I enter http://x.x.x.x (where x is the IP address assigned by the wireless provider), will remote access work? 3.b: If the Communication Module is used with a base module, can both devices be remotely configured and monitored? Thanks again.

The best approach is to consult the manual. [document]: [product_name] Communication Modules - Industrial Ethernet, [product_name] CMR2020, [product_name] CMR2040 Also, I'm not certain what you mean by 'SIM IP address'. Here is a link to relevant application examples (including VPN): [url]

The SIM IP address refers to the address assigned by your mobile network provider; it seems you interpreted 'SIM IP' without the full context 'SIM IP address assigned by wireless provider.' To summarize for others: Point 2: Yes Point 3.a: Yes Point 3.b: Yes

analysis.insight_summary: Users are asking about whether the [product_name] Communication Module can be used independently, its compatibility with all versions of the base module, and options for remote access via browser and VPN. Replies confirm the Communication Module's ability to function alone with basic I/O and SMS features, confirm any of the 8 [product_name] base modules (regardless of display) can be used, and clarify that both modules can be configured and monitored remotely. Reference to documentation and need for explicit info about remote connectivity was made.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect the Communication Module to work independently for SMS operations, to be compatible with any of the 8 base modules regardless of display, and to provide straightforward and secure remote access and configuration options for both modules.
